terms.comment: Greek μοναστήριον; a house of monks or of nuns. A convent of nuns is monastērium virginum (Cod. Just. 1.2.23, M-O).

terms.gloss: a house of monks or nuns living in common

phrases.latin: et erat monastērium Mediōlāniī plēnum bonīs frātribus extrā urbis moenia sub Ambrosiō nūtrītōre, et nōn nōverāmus
phrases.english: and there was a monastery at Milan, full of good brothers, outside the city walls, in Ambrose’s care, and we did not know it

sources: Lewis & Short: monasterium · Lewis & Short: coenobium
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. monastery, convent. Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 41, s.v. monastero.
Augustine, Confessions 8, checked against O’Donnell’s text in the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (9 November 2026).
